acceptance_criteria: No SmtpRelayQueue reference at call site. SMTP path unchanged. RoutingMailer failover tested. SES impl tested against mock. Feature flags compile cleanly.
close_reason: All 4 phases complete: OutboundMailer trait, SmtpRelayMailer, RoutingMailer, SES provider, health checking. 601 tests pass, clippy clean.
description:
## Why this issue exists

stoa-mail currently sends outbound mail through a single `SmtpRelayQueue` targeting one configured SMTP relay peer. The config already accepts `Vec<SmtpRelayPeerConfig>` but the delivery layer ignores all but the first. There is no abstraction that allows different provider types, no failover across peers, and no routing logic to select a provider per message.

Regulated and production deployments need: primary + fallback relay for resilience; HTTP API providers (SES, SendGrid, Mailgun, Postmark) for deliverability metrics, bounce integration, and suppression list management; and routing rules to send transactional mail through a different path than user-composed mail.

## What needs to be done

### Phase 1 — OutboundMailer trait

Define in `stoa-smtp` (or a new `stoa-outbound` crate):

```rust
pub struct OutboundEnvelope {
    pub mail_from: String,
    pub rcpt_to: Vec<String>,
    pub message: Bytes,          // RFC 5322 message bytes
    pub message_type: MessageType, // Transactional | Bulk | System
}

pub struct SendReceipt {
    pub provider_message_id: Option<String>,
    pub provider: &'static str,
}

#[async_trait]
pub trait OutboundMailer: Send + Sync {
    async fn send(&self, envelope: OutboundEnvelope) -> Result<SendReceipt, OutboundError>;
    fn name(&self) -> &'static str;
    fn healthy(&self) -> bool { true }
}
```

Migrate the existing `deliver_via_relay` path into a `SmtpRelayMailer` that implements this trait. `email/set.rs` receives `Arc<dyn OutboundMailer>` instead of `Option<&Arc<SmtpRelayQueue>>`.

### Phase 2 — RoutingMailer (failover + selection)

`RoutingMailer` wraps an ordered list of `(Selector, Arc<dyn OutboundMailer>)`:

- **Selector** matches on: recipient domain glob, `MessageType`, or catch-all
- On send: find first matching selector whose provider is healthy; attempt delivery; if it fails, fall through to next matching entry
- Emit per-provider Prometheus counters: `outbound_send_total{provider, result}`
- Emit `audit=true` tracing event on delivery failure with provider name and error

Config shape:
```toml
[[delivery.route]]
selector = { domain = "*.example.com" }
provider = "ses-primary"

[[delivery.route]]
selector = { type = "transactional" }
provider = "sendgrid"

[[delivery.route]]
selector = "*"
provider = "smtp-relay"
```

### Phase 3 — HTTP API provider implementations

Implement `OutboundMailer` for:

- **`SesMailer`**: AWS SES v2 `SendEmail` API (`aws-sdk-sesv2`). Authenticates via IAM role (no hardcoded credentials). Returns SES `MessageId` in `SendReceipt`.
- **`SendGridMailer`**: SendGrid Mail Send v3 API (`reqwest` + API key from secretx). 
- **`MailgunMailer`**: Mailgun Messages API (`reqwest` + API key from secretx).
- **`PostmarkMailer`**: Postmark Messages API (`reqwest` + server token from secretx).

Each impl is behind a Cargo feature flag (`ses`, `sendgrid`, `mailgun`, `postmark`) so unused providers don't pull in extra dependencies.

The existing `SmtpRelayMailer` (Phase 1) remains the default — no new dependencies required for a basic deployment.

### Phase 4 — Health checking

Add a background task that periodically sends a probe (or checks provider health API) for each configured provider and updates the `healthy()` state. `RoutingMailer` skips unhealthy providers without attempting delivery. Alert via Prometheus gauge `outbound_provider_healthy{provider}`.

## Acceptance criteria

- `email/set.rs` call site takes `Arc<dyn OutboundMailer>` — no reference to `SmtpRelayQueue`
- Existing SMTP relay path works through `SmtpRelayMailer` with no regression
- `RoutingMailer` selects provider by domain and message type; falls over to next on failure
- At least one HTTP API provider (SES) implemented and tested with a mock HTTP server
- Per-provider Prometheus counters present
- All new provider impls are behind feature flags

## Design notes

- Keep `SmtpRelayQueue` as the disk-backed queue for durability; `SmtpRelayMailer` drains it. HTTP API providers may use an in-memory queue with a configurable retry policy — disk durability is optional for providers that have their own retry logic.
- `OutboundError` should distinguish permanent failures (5xx, invalid address) from transient failures (connection refused, timeout) so `RoutingMailer` knows whether to retry or fail-fast.
- secretx integration for API keys: use the existing `secretx` workspace crate; keys are never in config files.
design: OutboundMailer trait is the correct seam. RoutingMailer composes N impls without any impl knowing about the others. Feature flags keep the binary size honest for deployments that only need SMTP relay.
title: Outbound mail: OutboundMailer trait + multi-provider routing
